screening_results.reason: This study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the bvFTD-focused meta-analysis. While it includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) and adequate sample size (10 bvFTD patients; I5), it does not use one of the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET): the study uses F-flortaucipir tau-PET (I3 not met). Critically, the paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) between-group contrasts for the bvFTD group (voxelwise SPM analyses were performed only for nfvPPA and CBS), so it fails to provide whole-brain group-level results clearly identified as coming from the target bvFTD sample (I6 and I7 not met). The full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are directly met, so exclusion is due to failure to satisfy required inclusion criteria I3, I6, and I7.

This empirical study (Lebreton et al., 2013) meets all inclusion criteria: it used VBM and task-based fMRI (I3); included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (both VBM sample n=48 and behavioral sample n=14–15) (I4, I5); reported between-group whole-brain voxelwise contrasts with MNI coordinates and statistical maps (e.g., AD vs bvFTD VBM comparisons with [x y z] MNI coordinates) (I6, I7); and whole-brain results are presented in figures and described in the text (I8). No exclusion criteria are met: the paper is an original empirical study (not a review), reports whole-brain analyses rather than ROI-only or seed-FC/DTI/cortical-thickness-only methods, and the patient selection/exclusion criteria do not indicate disqualifying comorbid psychiatric or substance-abuse samples. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete.

This study uses VBM and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=16) and adequate sample sizes, and reports whole-brain VBM results in MNI space; however, the VBM analyses reported are correlational across the entire sample (behavior–gray matter correlations) rather than a between-group voxelwise contrast specific to bvFTD. The paper does not present a clear group-level, whole-brain VBM contrast or voxelwise result explicitly identified as coming from the bvFTD group (e.g., bvFTD vs controls) in MNI/Talairach space. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7 which require at least one between-group contrast and at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise result clearly originating from the target sample group. No exclusion criteria were met.

The study includes VBM imaging and clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients with adequate sample size (bvFTD n=13), satisfying I3, I4 and I5. However, the VBM analyses are reported as voxel-wise correlations in a combined patient cohort (with syndromic group membership as a covariate) and the paper does not present a between-group contrast reported in stereotactic (MNI/Talairach) space specifically for the bvFTD group, nor a clear group-level, whole-brain voxelwise result identified as coming from the bvFTD sample. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria. It used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as an imaging modality (I3) and included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=22) (I4) with adequate group size (I5). The methods describe registration to MNI152 space and a voxelwise general linear model with TFCE and permutation testing; the authors report VBM group comparisons that replicate the visual-rating findings and refer to Supplementary Figures (online) showing the VBM results, indicating between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI space (I6). The paper reports group-level voxelwise (whole-brain/voxelwise) VBM results for the target groups (I7) and the VBM results are available in supplementary figures (I8). No exclusion criteria are met (no review/meta-analysis, not ROI-only, not disallowed modalities, and empirical original data). Full article text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary figures are referenced but missing here (acceptable).

This is an original empirical study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=12) that uses resting-state fMRI and voxel-based morphometry (VBM). It reports group-level between-group comparisons and whole-brain analyses using SPM with data normalized to MNI space, and describes voxelwise GM density reductions and resting-state network differences (with supplementary coordinate information). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (patients=12, controls=30). All required whole-brain, group-level results are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not only seed-based FC/DTI/cortical thickness, and sample exclusions for comorbidities were applied). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8. Exclusion criteria met: [].

This is an empirical case-control neuroimaging study that meets all inclusion criteria: it uses resting-state fMRI and voxel-based morphometry (I3); includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=21) (I4) with adequate group sizes (I5); reports voxelwise, between-group connectivity and atrophy comparisons with results referenced in stereotactic space (MNI seed coordinates are provided and voxelwise group maps/figures are reported) (I6); provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results for the target bvFTD group (I7) and presents results in figures/supplementary materials (I8). No exclusion criteria are met: this is not a review/meta-analysis, not ROI-only, not non-empirical, and does not rely solely on seed-based FC/DTI/cortical-thickness methods (it includes ICA/seed-based FC and VBM). The full text supplied includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

Study uses VBM and reports whole-brain, voxelwise atrophy analyses (SPM99 VBM) normalized to Talairach coordinates, with cluster-level results—satisfying imaging and whole-brain reporting requirements. Sample includes 29 clinically diagnosed FTD patients, specifically subgroups of 15 with primary progressive aphasia and 14 with a disorder of social and executive functioning; the latter corresponds to behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) by clinical description, fulfilling the bvFTD sample requirement. Group sizes exceed the minimum (FTD n=29; controls n=12). Between-group contrasts and naming-atrophy correlations are reported in stereotactic space (Talairach) and voxelwise, meeting coordinate-reporting criteria. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not DTI/FC/cortical-thickness-only, and sample exclusions not violated). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study is excluded because it reports only region-of-interest volumetric analyses of amygdala subnuclei derived from T1-weighted structural MRI rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET, and it does not report whole-brain voxelwise/group-level coordinate results. Exclusion ID met: E3 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion IDs met: I5 (sample size criterion: 132 patients and 107 controls). Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (imaging modality is T1 structural segmentation, not VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET), I4 (the paper does not specifically report results for a clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD subgroup), I6 (no between-group results reported in MNI/Talairach coordinates), I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level results reported). Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

Exclusion based on imaging and analysis methods: the study uses structural MRI cortical thickness/ROI analyses (FreeSurfer Desikan–Killiany labels) rather than VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET, and it reports ROI-based cortical volume/thickness results rather than whole-brain voxelwise coordinates in MNI/Talairach space. Therefore it meets exclusion criteria E3 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) and E6 (reports cortical thickness methods rather than acceptable imaging modalities). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample present) and I5 (sample sizes ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (required imaging modality VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group results reported in standard stereotaxic coordinates), and I7 (no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete.

Study meets inclusion criteria: uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3); participants were clinically diagnosed with behavioral variant FTD/FTLD and recruited using research criteria (I4); sample sizes are 7 and 10 in patient subgroups and matched controls (~17), satisfying minimum N≥6 (I5); analyses report between-group voxelwise contrasts using normalization to the MNI template (I6); results are whole-brain, group-level voxelwise VBM comparisons for target groups (I7); reporting of whole-brain results in text/figures meets allowance for coordinates/figures (I8). No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not excluded comorbidities, and uses whole-brain VBM). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

The study uses VBM (I3) and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=15) (I4) with adequate group sizes (I5). Voxel-wise analyses are reported and MNI coordinates are referenced (I6, I8). However, the reported whole-brain VBM results pertain to (a) a mixed-diagnosis subgroup defined by poor melody scores versus controls and (b) covariate-based correlations across all patients; the paper does not present a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast that is clearly identified as coming specifically from the bvFTD group. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I7 (whole-brain result for the target sample). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete. Exclusion is based on unmet I7 while I3, I4, I5, I6, and I8 are satisfied.

This empirical study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality, includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (Neary criteria), has adequate sample size (103 patients reviewed, 91 with usable imaging), and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results in standardized space (MNI coordinates provided, with FWE-corrected and uncorrected statistical maps). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and reports group-level whole-brain VBM findings (right ventral putamen/pallidum) suitable for coordinate-based meta-analysis. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the paper should be included.

This study meets several inclusion criteria: it uses VBM (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=27) (I4), has adequate sample sizes (>6) in patient and control groups (I5), and reports between-group contrasts with coordinates in MNI space (I6). It also provides whole-brain voxelwise results presented in figures/tables (I8). However, the key requirement I7 is not satisfied: the paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) result that is clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD group alone. The VBM correlational result that survives correction is reported across all patient groups combined; the authors explicitly state that the correlation in each diagnostic group (including bv-FTD) did not show any region surviving correction. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete for screening.

This is a single-case clinical report (one patient) using 18F-FDG PET. Inclusion criterion I3 is satisfied (FDG-PET used). However the study does not meet multiple required inclusion criteria: I4 (sample does not consist of a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group — the paper reports a single FTLD/bvFTD-like case), I5 (sample size <6; only one patient), I6 (no between-group contrasts reported in MNI/Talairach space), and I7 (no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results from a target sample group). No exclusion criteria from the provided list are triggered (e.g., it is empirical and not a review). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails to meet required inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I7.

The study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8: it uses VBM and resting-state fMRI; includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (N=87, subgroups 21 and 66); reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with MNI coordinates; and provides figures/tables of whole-brain contrasts. However, it violates exclusion criterion E4 because some participants had histories of alcohol and drug abuse (reported 4/21 CB-bvFTD patients), meaning the sample is not free of substance-abuse comorbidity. No other exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded per E4.

This is an observational cohort prognostic study without any neuroimaging analyses of the types required. Although the sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=64) and sample sizes exceed 6, the paper does not use VBM, task or resting-state fMRI, or FDG-PET (I3 not met), and it does not report any between-group voxelwise contrasts or coordinates in MNI/Talairach space (I6, I7 not met). No whole-brain group-level voxelwise imaging results or coordinate tables/figures are provided (I8 not met). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study does not meet the imaging and whole-brain reporting inclusion criteria required for this review.

This study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the bvFTD-focused meta-analysis. Satisfied: I3 (uses VBM preprocessing/tissue segmentation and modulated GM maps) and I5 (FTD sample size reported; test set FTD n=12, HC n=18, meeting the >=6 threshold). Not satisfied: I4 — the paper includes 'FTD' without specifying clinical subtype (bvFTD not explicitly identified), so it does not confirm inclusion of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients; I6 and I7 — the manuscript reports multivariate classification results (AUC, SVM decision values) and radar/ROC plots but does not present between-group voxelwise univariate contrasts with coordinates in MNI/Talairach space or clear whole-brain voxelwise group-level statistical maps/tables. No exclusion criteria from the list (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET modality used), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed behavioural-variant FTD patients), I5 (>=6 participants in patient group; 20 FTD patients). This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) whole-brain analyses (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=19) (I4), has sufficient sample sizes (bvFTD n=19, controls n=25) (I5), reports results with MNI coordinates (I6), and provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise findings clearly attributed to the bvFTD sample (I7) with tables/figures described in the text (I8). The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods (VBM details), Results (voxelwise associations with MNI coords), and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review; not ROI-only; not only seed-FC/DTI/thickness; no evidence of disqualifying comorbid samples).

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (bvFTD n=26) and meets the minimum sample-size requirement, it does not use one of the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET). Instead, the neuroimaging methods are ROI-based volumetric analyses using FreeSurfer cortical parcellation. The paper does not report whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results in a stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) or coordinate tables/figures; results are presented as ROI volumetric associations. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I3, I6, and I7 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete. Exclusion is based on E3; inclusion criteria met: I4, I5; inclusion criteria not met: I3, I6, I7.

Although this study used resting-state fMRI (I3) and included clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants within an FTD subgroup (I4), and has adequate sample size in the healthy control group (N=10) satisfying the >=6 participant threshold (I5), the paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results for a combined FTD group (mixed bvFTD, svPPA, nfvPPA) rather than providing whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results specifically for behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) alone. The meta-analysis objective targets bvFTD-specific whole-brain results. Therefore inclusion criterion I7 (whole-brain results clearly identified as coming from the target sample group — bvFTD) is not met. No exclusion criteria from the provided list (E2, E3, E4, E5, E6) apply. Because I7 is not satisfied, the study must be excluded from the bvFTD meta-analysis.

This empirical study meets all inclusion criteria for the bvFTD imaging meta-analysis. It used FDG-PET (I3) and explicitly recruited patients diagnosed with the frontal/behavioral variant of FTD (bvFTD) (I4). Sample sizes exceed minimum thresholds (142 clinical patients overall; PET subgroup N=41; healthy comparison N=16) satisfying I5. Voxelwise, whole-brain SPM analyses were performed and reported, with results given in stereotactic coordinates (Talairach) and figures (I6, I7, I8). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) contrasts (patients vs. controls; H1 vs H2) with corrected and uncorrected thresholds and cluster coordinates. No exclusion criteria are met: the study is not a review/meta-analysis (E2), did not restrict to ROI-only analyses (E3), excluded comorbid psychiatric/other dementia diagnoses per methods (thus does not violate E4), is empirical (not E5), and did not use only seed-based FC/DTI/cortical thickness (E6). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore INCLUDE.

The study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (meets I3) and included >6 patients (overall N=65; FTD n=11) (meets I5). However it does not clearly report inclusion of clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) specifically—patients are reported as “FTD” without subtype specification (I4 not met). The provided full text does not present between-group contrast results with coordinates in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) for a bvFTD group (I6 not met), nor does it clearly report a whole-brain, group-level voxelwise result identified as coming from a bvFTD target sample (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria from the list are triggered based on the provided text. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded for failing to meet all required inclusion criteria related to bvFTD-specific reporting.

This is an empirical VBM study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup and reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts with stereotactic coordinates. Imaging modality: VBM (I3). The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) and the study has sufficient sample size in at least one group (25 healthy controls; I5). The paper reports between-group contrasts with MNI-style coordinates and detailed SPM results (I6), and provides whole-brain voxelwise group-level results for the bvFTD clinical subgroup (I7). Results and coordinates are reported in text/figures/tables (I8). Full text (methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met. The study is therefore eligible for inclusion in the bvFTD imaging meta-analysis.

This is an empirical study that used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3) and included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=19) (I4) with adequate sample size (≥6) in patient and control groups (I5). The paper reports voxel-wise, whole-brain VBM analyses in MNI space and presents group-level anatomical results (including whole-brain significant clusters and ROI-corrected findings) in figures/tables (satisfying I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria (systematic review, ROI-only reporting, non-empirical study, prohibited imaging modality, or documented comorbid psychiatric/other dementia confounds) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are met.

Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET modality), I5 (sample size ≥6 for patient group: FTD n=13), I6 (between-group voxelwise contrasts reported in Talairach space), I7 (whole-brain/group-level voxelwise results for the FTD group), I8 (results presented as maps/patterns). This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) for whole-brain voxel-wise analyses (SPM/DARTEL normalized to MNI space) and reports group-level between-group contrasts (bvFTD vs controls) with voxelwise results and coordinate tables/figures (including peak left anterior insula). The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=82) and healthy controls (n=80), exceeding the minimum sample size. The paper provides stage-specific and whole-brain voxelwise results clearly identified as coming from the target bvFTD sample. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and is sufficiently complete for screening.

This is an empirical VBM study that includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and reports voxelwise, whole-brain between-group contrasts. Methods: SPM5 VBM processing and whole-brain analyses are described. Sample: bvFTD groups (bvFTD(CBD) N=5, bvFTD(Pick’s) N=5) and healthy controls N=53 (controls >6 satisfying sample-size criterion). Results: VBM group-level comparisons vs. controls and direct bvFTD group comparisons are reported (figures and Table 2) at voxelwise thresholds (FWE-corrected and uncorrected), consistent with reporting in a defined stereotaxic space via SPM5 (MNI space). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results are clearly identified for the target bvFTD samples. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Figures/Tables; fulltext appears complete.

Exclusion: E6 (study uses cortical thickness vertex-wise structural MRI analyses rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients included), I5 (sample sizes: 88 bvFTD patients and 30 controls, >6), I7 (whole-brain, vertex-by-vertex cortical thickness analyses reported at the group level). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality requirement — paper uses cortical thickness, not VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET), I6 (no explicit reporting of between-group results in a defined stereotaxic coordinate space such as MNI or Talairach in the provided text). Although whole-brain vertexwise results and group comparisons are described and figures/maps are reported, the study does not satisfy the modality requirement and appears to report cortical-thickness maps rather than coordinate-based VBM/FDG-PET/fMRI contrasts required by the review. Therefore it must be excluded.

This is an empirical VBM study of patients with frontotemporal dementia (described as frontal-variant/FTD), meeting the meta-analysis target of behavioral-variant FTD. Imaging modality: voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3). Sample: includes 13 FTD patients (6 overeaters) and 47 controls; MRI analyses used 27 patients and 47 controls (>=6 participants satisfied) (I5). The paper reports between-group, voxelwise contrasts (overeaters vs nonovereaters and controls) with stereotactic coordinates reported (e.g., x=41,y=12,z=-13; x=43,y=1,z=-7; x=19,y=65,z=-18), satisfying coordinate reporting (I6). Whole-brain voxelwise VBM results identifying right ventral insula, striatum, and orbitofrontal cortex at p<0.05 corrected within the ROI are reported as group-level, voxelwise findings originating from the target sample (I7). Results are presented in figures/tables and discussed in text (I8). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study is excluded because it does not meet the imaging modality requirement (I3) and does not provide whole-brain voxelwise results specifically for the target bvFTD group (I7). The study uses longitudinal structural MRI with tensor-based morphometry (TBM) and boundary-shift integral, not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET, so I3 is not satisfied. Although the sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4 met) and sample sizes exceed 6 (I5 met), the voxelwise comparisons presented are between genetic FTD subgroups rather than a bvFTD versus control between-group contrast reported in a defined stereotactic space for the target sample (I6/I7 not satisfied). Additionally, the sample includes cases with comorbid neurological disorder (FTD with ALS), violating exclusion criterion E4. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the paper must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This study uses resting-state fMRI (AAL parcellation) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=41) with healthy controls (n=39), meeting I3, I4, and I5. However, analyses are ROI-based network/MST comparisons using AAL regions and report node-level and edge-level differences (region IDs and AAL coordinates in figures), but they do not report voxelwise, whole-brain between-group contrast peak coordinates in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 (at least one between-group voxelwise contrast reported in MNI/Talairach and a group-level whole-brain voxelwise result) are not met. Per exclusion criterion E3 (studies reporting only ROI analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results), the paper must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

The study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and SPM/DARTEL (I3), includes clinically diagnosed behavioural variant FTD patients within the cohort (I4), has sufficient sample sizes (42 patients, 35 controls) (I5), and reports voxel-based morphometry group-level whole-brain analyses with coordinate-referenced maps (I6,I8). This study reports empirical resting-state fMRI and VBM analyses in a clinical sample of 19 bvFTD patients and 19 controls. This empirical study used FDG-PET with voxel-based (SPM8) whole-brain analyses, included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=26) and controls/AD, and reports voxelwise between-group contrasts normalized to MNI space (SPM, reported cluster/BA results and supplementary tables). This is an empirical longitudinal study that includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=12) and uses resting-state fMRI and voxel-based morphometry (VBM). This empirical resting-state fMRI study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=8) and healthy controls (n=16), meeting sample-size requirements. This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=35) (I4) with adequate sample sizes (bvFTD n=35, controls n=29) (I5), reports voxel-wise between-group contrasts and VBM correlations in MNI space with peak coordinates referenced in Supplementary Table 3 (I6), and provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results identified for the bvFTD sample (I7). This is an empirical VBM study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=34) with healthy controls (n=30). Sample sizes exceed the minimum. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets imaging modality (VBM), clinical sample, sample size, between-group voxelwise results in stereotaxic space (via reported supplementary tables), and whole-brain evidence.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses VBM (SPM99) (I3); includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients with behavioral symptoms consistent with behavioral-variant FTD and explicitly excluded primary aphasias (I4); sample size is 9 FTD patients and 26 controls (meets I5); reports voxelwise, whole-brain SPM results and provides stereotactic coordinates (e.g., (0, -28, -10)) (I6); presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results clearly attributed to the patient group (I7); and whole-brain results are reported in the text/figures/tables (I8). No exclusion criteria are met (no review/meta-analysis, not ROI-only, empirical VBM study, no disallowed modalities). Full text appears complete (includes intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an original empirical study that uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and FDG-PET imaging, includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=23; n=21 in MRI analysis after QC), reports whole-brain voxelwise SPM results with stereotactic coordinates converted between MNI and Talairach, and presents group-level voxelwise comparisons vs. controls and vs. bipolar disorder. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical FDG-PET study using voxel-wise SPM analysis (whole-brain) of 29 clinically diagnosed frontotemporal dementia patients (specified as FTD and excluding PNFA/semantic dementia), and 11 healthy controls. It reports group-level voxelwise between-group contrasts with MNI/Talairach coordinates (Table 3) and whole-brain SPM results (figures and tables). Sample sizes exceed the minimum. This study meets all inclusion criteria: it includes clinically diagnosed behavioural-variant FTD patients (n=12) (I4), uses FDG-PET as an imaging modality alongside ASL (I3), has adequate sample size (≥6 in patient group) (I5), reports voxel-wise between-group contrasts using SPM normalized to MNI space with MNI coordinates and cluster tables/figures (I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This empirical study met all required inclusion criteria: it investigated behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) patients, used voxel-based morphometry (MRI VBM) and 18F-FDG PET (I3), included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (selected as patients who converted to probable bvFTD; I4), had adequate sample sizes (25 patients, 20 controls; I5), and reported voxelwise, whole-brain between-group contrasts with Talairach-coordinate tables and SPM analyses (I6, I7, I8). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (E2, E3, E4, E5, E6) are triggered: the paper is primary empirical work, reports whole-brain voxelwise results (not ROI-only or seed-based FC/DTI/cortical-thickness-only), and excluded participants with major psychiatric/other neurological disorders. The study is an empirical, task-based fMRI investigation of music and vocal emotion processing in clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=15) versus healthy controls (n=11). It reports between-group voxelwise contrasts analyzed in SPM with normalization to MNI space and presents group-level whole-brain results (e.g., musical mode variation: controls > bvFTD, P < 0.05 FWE whole-brain) as well as small-volume corrected findings. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets the review’s imaging modality requirement (task fMRI), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample, satisfies the sample size threshold, reports between-group contrasts in MNI space, and provides at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise result from the target sample. No exclusion criteria are met.

The study is excluded because it does not include clinically diagnosed behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) patients (I4 not met). Study strengths vs criteria: It uses voxel-based morphometry (SPM12) satisfying I3; has adequate sample size (n=104) satisfying I5; reports whole-brain voxelwise group analyses (voxel-based comparisons) satisfying I7; and presents group-level whole-brain results in figures/effect maps satisfying I8. However, the paper does not identify any bvFTD patient group in the participant diagnoses (baseline diagnoses listed: PSP, PPAOS, LPA, nfvPPA, SD, etc.), so I4 is not met. Additionally, the provided full text does not include explicit coordinate tables (MNI or Talairach) or coordinate listings for between-group contrasts, so I6 is not clearly met. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) were triggered based on the provided full text. Given that all inclusion criteria must be met and I4 (and likely I6) are not satisfied, the study must be excluded from the bvFTD meta-analysis.

Thus it meets all required inclusion criteria (VBM modality, bvFTD sample, n>=6, between-group contrasts in MNI space, and whole-brain group-level voxelwise results). No exclusion criteria apply: this is not a review, not ROI-only, participants with psychiatric comorbidity were excluded, and the study includes VBM (not only DTI or FC). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).
